answer: Stake-weighted identity bonds priced like a tundra option book make each new agent post collateral whose slashing cost exceeds the expected sybil payoff. An inlet of cheap identities gets repriced by a bonding-curve premium, so N fake agents cost N times a convex fee, not a flat toll. That nectar of honest spread covers verification, but colluding whales can still amortize across many identities, capping the defense.
